text:
Alex T.: Heads-up — canary for release/2026-03 runtime merge is showing a p95 decode spike (~+22%) on short-seq traffic after the merge landed. Notably saw this on two different instance shapes.
Sophia Y.: saw it too on canary-3 around 09:14 UTC. p50 fine, p95 and p99 blown up.
Raj P.: any obvious kernel switch in the traces?
Alex T.: attaching quick flame sample (copied output):
```
flamegraph: decode_fastpath
---
40% runtime::decode::attention_fused_kernel_v2
18% runtime::kv_cache::lookup
10% cuda::matmul::fused_matmul
8% runtime::batcher::schedule
```
Looks like attention_fused_kernel_v2 dominating.
Emily S.: interesting — our kernel selector heuristic was updated in this merge to prefer fused kernels for seq_len<=64 when batch>1. Could be warmup/affinity interaction with the batcher.
Sophia Y.: here's the selector diff from the merge (lines):
```diff
- if (seq_len <= 32 && batch_size <= 4) use_attn_fallback();
+ if (seq_len <= 64 && batch_size <= 8) prefer_fused_attn();
```
That change landed in commit 8a7b9c3.
Raj P.: rolling test logs show a lot more kv-cache evictions during canary runs. snippet: `kv_eviction_count: 348 -> 912` over 10m. Could be short seqs bumping batch sizes and pushing early KV spills.
Alex T.: I ran a focused profile with explicit kernel selection pinned to fallback kernel and p95 dropped back to baseline. So this is pretty suspicious.
perf-bot: CI perf comparison for canary-2026-03-12: p95_decode: baseline=38ms, canary=46ms (+21%), p99_decode: baseline=92ms, canary=115ms (+25%).
Emily S.: does the fused kernel have hidden memory copies or extra memsets for some shapes? I recall a small extra memcpy added to align keys when batch>1.
Sophia Y.: yes — there is a KV layout path that pads keys to 64-byte boundaries inside the fused kernel. That code path executes only when `prefer_fused_attn` enabled.
Alex T.: suggestion: revert the selector change (8a7b9c3) or make it conditional on `kv_cache_pressure==low`. We need a revert candidate for rollout hold.
Raj P.: bisect plan: try revert selector change first (fast), if that fixes perf, we can roll that out and do deeper follow-up on fused kernel memcopy. Volunteers to run canary?
Emily S.: I'll push a revert PR to test on canary-3.
Sophia Y.: I can run a KV-heavy synthetic to confirm evictions go down. I'll post numbers.
perf-bot: Snapshot created: revert-test-452900-1 at 4529004450.
deploy-bot: rollout to canary paused for release/2026-03 (held by eng-runtime).
Alex T.: if revert fixes, we should still follow up with a microbenchmark of fused kernel vs fallback for small seqs and check memory traffic counters (L2, dram). Raj can you add nvprof counters?
Raj P.: on it — adding mem_bandwidth and dram_read/write counters. Will push samples in ~20m.
Emily S.: FYI, if we do a revert, we'll need to update the changelog and call out the KV pressure caveat. We should also set a guard in selector config for QPS>threshold.
Sophia Y.: after the revert run: kv_eviction_count dropped 912 -> 360 over same 10m window, p95 back to 39ms. Looks promising.
Alex T.: great — I'll open a follow-up issue to rework fused kernel path (avoid memcopy, respect KV layout) instead of permanently disabling fused kernels.
Emily S.: opening issue #INF-1429 with initial triage notes and profiling artifacts.
Raj P.: uploaded nvprof snippet: `dram_read_bytes: canary=1.9GB -> baseline=1.1GB` when fused path chosen. That explains latency.
Alex T.: summary: roll back selector change, hold rollout, create follow-up to optimize fused kernel memory path and make selector KV-pressure-aware. Thanks all. :thumbsup: 
Sophia Y.: thanks — will keep monitoring canary once revert PR merges.
perf-bot: revert PR perf run complete: p95 back within 3% of baseline.
deploy-bot: release/2026-03 remains paused until ENG-Runtime approves.
Alex T.: leaving this thread open until follow-up PRs are merged.
